selection_reasoning: These 4 tasks form a coherent multi-hop sequence. The player must first locate birch_fence and tnt as navigation/exploration tasks that lead them to resource areas. Finding gray_concrete nearby allows them to mine it, and once they have gathered concrete blocks, they can build a tower. This creates a logical progression from exploration → resource gathering → construction. The tasks are observable, verifiable, and don't require deep crafting knowledge (no complex recipe chains). The 'find' tasks serve as prerequisites that guide the player to the right area, mining provides building materials, and the tower is the final construction goal.

edges.reason: Gray concrete is placed near the birch fence area; player must navigate there first to locate the mineable blocks
TNT serves as a landmark near the concrete deposit; finding it confirms the player is in the correct mining zone
Building a tower requires blocks obtained from mining gray concrete; mined blocks become the construction material

milestones.description: Uses position_near_with_facing because this is a find/locate task. The player must navigate to within 5 blocks of the birch fence cluster center (spawn-relative 7, 0, 6) and face toward it. max_distance reduced from 16 to 5 per CommonSenseAgent/ValidatorAgent feedback — the fence is ~9 blocks from spawn, so max_distance=5 forces the player to walk at least 4 blocks toward it rather than potentially satisfying the condition from spawn.

Uses position_near_with_facing because this is a find/locate task. The player must navigate to within 5 blocks of the TNT stack center (spawn-relative 10, 0, 10) and face toward it. max_distance reduced from 16 to 5 per CommonSenseAgent/ValidatorAgent feedback — the TNT is ~14.5 blocks from spawn, so max_distance=5 forces the player to walk at least 9.5 blocks toward it, ensuring meaningful navigation.

Uses inventory_has because mining gray concrete with a pickaxe causes it to drop as an item into the player's inventory. The diamond pickaxe is provided in the scene. Requiring min_count=4 ensures meaningful mining occurred and provides enough material for the subsequent tower-building task. This is preferred over mine_block event tracking because inventory_has directly confirms the player possesses the building material needed for the next task.

Uses count_in_box_at_least (kind=block) because building a tower means placing blocks in the world. The box starts at Y=3 (spawn-relative) to EXCLUDE the pre-existing gray concrete structure which occupies Y=0 to Y=2. This ensures only player-placed blocks are detected. The generous XZ range (-5 to 22) covers the entire buildable area. Requiring min_count=4 confirms a tower of at least 4 blocks tall was constructed above the existing structures.

scene_description: A flat grass platform with three distinct landmarks arranged in increasing distance from spawn: a birch fence enclosure (6-8 blocks away), a TNT stack (10-11 blocks away), and a large gray concrete structure (13-16 blocks away). The player is given a diamond pickaxe to mine the concrete and build a tower on the open grass. The landmarks guide exploration through the scene toward the mining zone.
task_text: Explore the area to find the birch fence and TNT landmarks, then mine the gray concrete structure with your diamond pickaxe, and use the mined blocks to build a tower at least 4 blocks tall.
design_notes: Layout (spawn-relative coordinates): Player spawns at (0,0,0). Birch fence U-shape at (6-8, 0, 5-7). TNT 2x2x2 stack at (10-11, 0-1, 10). Gray concrete 4x3x4 cube at (13-16, 0-2, 5-8) = 48 blocks. Open grass everywhere for tower placement. Diamond pickaxe provided for mining. Air cleared to Y=10 to ensure no obstructions. The /fill for grass_block at Y=-1 creates the floor, and air fill removes any natural blocks that might interfere.
